To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
BDNF is synthesized and stored by mouse neurons as the mature, biologically active form, not as the precursor, pro-BDNF.
BDNF in neurons exists in a precursor (pro-BDNF) and mature (mature BDNF) form and that mature BDNF is released in response to neuronal activity.

pro- and mature BNF are present in neurons in a dynamic equilibrium, that the pro-BDNF pool is rapidly and efficiently converted to the mature form, and that the mature BDNF pool is stored and released in response to excitatory input.
In summary, our research is concerned with

understanding how BDNF is synthesized, processed, and secreted by neurons, how these processes are affected by disease and aging, and how they contribute to the pathophysiology of neurological disorders.
the molecular mechanisms of neuronal survival and death, and with the role that the neurotrophins play in these processes.
the molecular and cellular mechanisms of neurotrophic factors and their receptors in the developing and mature brain.
